title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Γ = Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) acts by outer automorphisms on π1 of the moduli stack M_{1,1} over Q̄. This group is SL(2,Z)^, the profinite completion of SL(2,Z). Its congruence quotient is SL(2,Ẑ). Formula (7), on an earlier page, is presumably the congruence map SL(2,Z)^ → SL(2,Ẑ), whose kernel is the congruence kernel.

Previous page. The cusp at infinity of M_{1,1,Q} gives an inertia group T = T_∞ ≅ Ẑ(1). This gives a conjugacy class of homomorphisms κ: T → SL(2,Z)^ (formula 8). Its image in SL(2,Ẑ) is, up to conjugation, the unipotent group {(1 0; n 1) : n ∈ Ẑ} (formula 9). Γ respects this class and so acts on T through a character χ: Γ → Aut(T) = Ẑ*, which is the cyclotomic character (formula 10).

This page.
1. The general statement is diagram (11). Take any outer automorphism u of SL(2,Z)^ that preserves the conjugacy class of κ(T). Then there should be a unique χ(u) ∈ Aut(T) = Ẑ* with κ∘χ(u) = u∘κ, up to conjugation.
2. He offers a variant ('ou mieux, seulement dans…') with SL(2,Ẑ) in place of SL(2,Z)^, and an outer automorphism ũ of SL(2,Ẑ).
3. This gives a character χ on the subgroup of Out(SL(2,Ẑ)) (resp. Out(SL(2,Z)^)) of inertia-preserving outer automorphisms. The arithmetic Γ_Q lies in that subgroup, and the cyclotomic character is the restriction of this purely group-theoretic character.
4. Moreover Γ lies in a smaller subgroup: outer automorphisms that also preserve the kernel of (7), and that act (as outer automorphisms) on the quotient SL(2,Ẑ) through the composite Γ → Ẑ* → Ẑ*/Ẑ*² → Autext_loc(SL(2,Ẑ)). Concretely, Galois acts on torsion points via conjugation by diag(χ,1) in GL(2,Ẑ). Conjugation by g ∈ GL(2,Ẑ) is inner on SL(2,Ẑ) iff det g ∈ Ẑ*² (using scalar matrices). So the outer action factors through Ẑ*/Ẑ*².
5. Last remark, continued on the next page. The centre {±1} of SL(2,Z)^ is nontrivial, so the outer action does not by itself reconstitute the extension N_{1,1} of Γ_Q by SL(2,Z)^. It only determines the extension by SL(2,Z)^/{±1}. That extension is then identified with the genus-0 extension attached to M_{0,4}.

Purpose. This is the first step towards a genus-1 analogue of the description of Γ_Q (or of GT) inside the outer automorphisms of π1(M_{1,1}). The conditions are: preserve cusp inertia with a character, preserve the congruence kernel, and act on the congruence quotient in a prescribed way.
errors: Uniqueness of χ(u) is fine for SL(2,Z)^, where the normalizer of the closed cusp subgroup is plausibly only ±Û. It fails for the SL(2,Ẑ) variant (11'). There, inner conjugation by diag(a,a⁻¹) ∈ SL(2,Ẑ) normalizes the unipotent subgroup and acts on it by a^{-2}. So for an outer automorphism class of SL(2,Ẑ), χ(u) is only determined modulo Ẑ*². The 'better' version with SL(2,Ẑ) therefore gives a character only into Ẑ*/Ẑ*², which is consistent with the Ẑ*/Ẑ*² appearing a few lines later.
The square (11) commutes only up to inner automorphism; κ is a conjugacy class of homomorphisms, not a homomorphism. This is implicit in the notes.

'Autext_loc!' is not defined on the page. If it means locally inner (inner modulo every level n), note that conjugation by diag(a,1) is not inner modulo n when a is a non-square mod n. The intended meaning is unclear.

ideas.what: Galois action on the cusp inertia of π1(M_{1,1}) recovers the cyclotomic character. Any outer automorphism preserving the inertia class determines a 'cyclotomic-type' character, so Γ_Q sits in the inertia-preserving subgroup of Out(SL(2,Z)^).
ideas.modern_name: inertia-preserving (cuspidal) outer automorphisms of the profinite modular group; genus-1 / elliptic GT conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura (1990s, Galois rigidity and exterior representations of SL(2,Z)^ and genus-1 braid groups); Ihara for genus 0; later Hain–Matsumoto and Enriquez (elliptic GT)
ideas.where_published: Theme of SL(2,Z)^ and M_{1,1} in La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse (1984), without this explicit formalism as far as I know

ideas.what: Γ_Q preserves the congruence kernel and acts on SL(2,Ẑ) by outer automorphisms factoring through Ẑ*/Ẑ*² (conjugation by diag(χ,1) modulo inner automorphisms).
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on torsion / congruence quotient of π1(M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Weil pairing, Galois action on elliptic curve torsion)

ideas.what: The centre ±1 obstructs recovering the extension from the outer action. One passes to PSL, and SL(2,Z)^/{±1} is related to the M_{0,4} / M_{0,3}-extension, with SL(2,Z/2) ≅ S_3 as quotient.
ideas.modern_name: relation M_{1,1} vs M_{0,4} via Legendre level 2; extension classes and centres
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; used by Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura

deep.surprise_reason: These are careful but standard observations on the Galois outer action on π1(M_{1,1}): cusp inertia gives the cyclotomic character, and the congruence quotient action factors through Ẑ*/Ẑ*². They were later developed systematically by Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and others. Their value is historical, as an early formulation of genus-1 'Teichmüller tower' conditions, not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: 'd'où une condition χ (10)' is more plausibly 'd'où un caractère χ (10)', with χ inserted above the line.
'qui ont la propriété voisin[?] gén.[?]' is likely 'qui ont la propriété envisagée'.
'normalisent[?] le noyau de (7)' is more likely 'invarient le noyau de (7)'.
'groupe des tous les automorph.' should read 'groupe de tous les automorph. ext. u'.
'— ou mieux, seulement des' is probably '— ou mieux, seulement dans'.
'Ẑ*/Ẑ*²_c' denotes the quotient by the squares (the subscript is unclear).
